value.body: A four-year degree covering crop production, soil science, plant protection, horticulture, agricultural economics and extension. The final year includes field work in villages and industry (Rural Agricultural Work Experience). It is offered mainly by state agricultural universities, with a course structure set by ICAR guidelines.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 8 semesters, including rural and industry work experience

items.label: Students enrolled
items.note: All modes; recorded as B.Agri. Some B.Sc (Hons) Agriculture students may be counted under B.Sc (Hons)

items.label: Agriculture & allied universities
items.note: Universities of this type that responded to the survey

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Mathematics; some universities also accept Agriculture as a subject. ICAR fills 20% of the All India Quota seats in agricultural universities, and all seats at a few ICAR and central institutions, through CUET-UG (ICAR counselling). Other seats go through state tests such as KCET, AP/TS EAPCET and MHT-CET, or university tests.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many state agriculture department posts ask for an agriculture degree specifically.
Private-sector work is mostly in seeds, fertilisers, agrochemicals, food processing and rural finance.
An M.Sc (Agriculture) through ICAR AIEEA-PG is a common next step.
